answers.answer: Choose 3 Escape Pod tokens in a four-player game. Place the lowest-numbered pod in Section A, the next-numbered in B, then alternate A/B; all start Locked side up. The bag starts with 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults plus 1 additional Adult per player, so 7 Adults with four players.
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 7 and 10: 3 pods for 3–4 players; lowest-numbered in A, next in B, alternate, Locked side up; bag formula lists 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults plus one per player.

answers.answer: Remove Corporate and Personal Objective cards that show a player count above the actual player count, shuffle the decks separately, and deal each player one from each deck. Each player chooses one of their two at the First Encounter—the first time an Intruder miniature appears—and removes the rejected one face down unseen from the game. Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this choice.
answers.evidence: Setup step 16; Special Rules, Critical gameplay moments: First Encounter triggers the choice; the rejected Objective is removed face down, and Eggs do not trigger it.

answers.answer: Discard the used Action card and two additional Action cards to pay its printed cost of 2. Contamination cards cannot pay any Action cost, so the two held Contamination cards cannot substitute. If the Action card has sections separated by OR, choose one section to use.
answers.evidence: Actions: Action card is discarded plus required additional cards; Contamination cards can never pay costs; choose one section when a card has OR.

answers.answer: They suffer 1 Light Wound at the end of their own round, after taking their one Action and passing. Once passed, they cannot act again that Player Phase, but may discard any number of cards when passing. Later players' rounds do not burn them again; the Fire damage rule applies to a Character at the end of that Character's own round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Player rounds: ending a round in Fire causes 1 Light Wound; passing bars further Actions and permits discarding any number of cards; damage is after finishing their own round.

answers.answer: On entering, flip the unexplored Room tile face up, reveal and resolve its Exploration token, then remove that token to the box. Set the Room's Item count by rotating the tile so the token number faces the printed Item Counter (except Nest and Room Covered in Slime). Resolve the token effect: Silence suppresses the Noise roll; Danger suppresses it and moves all eligible neighboring Intruders into the Room, or places Noise in each connected corridor lacking a marker if none are eligible; other listed effects place Slime, Fire, Malfunction, or a Door as directed. If no effect suppresses the roll, an empty destination gets a Noise roll. A destination already containing a Character or Intruder gets no Noise roll. A Noise roll of Silence does nothing unless Slime turns it into Danger.
answers.evidence: Movement, Rooms, and Corridors; Exploration tokens; Noise roll: entering reveals the tile/token; Item count is set from the token; Silence and Danger suppress a roll; do not roll if another Character or Intruder is already there.

answers.answer: Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards and replaces the post-move Noise roll with placing a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the destination. It is forbidden while in Combat and when every Corridor connected to the destination already has a Noise marker. It follows normal movement restrictions, so a Closed Door blocks crossing; miniatures cannot stop in Corridors.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions: Careful Movement; Movement, Rooms, and Corridors: no one may stop in a Corridor and Closed Doors block neighboring status for player movement.

answers.answer: If a Noise roll instructs placing a marker in a Corridor that already has one, resolve an Encounter. A marker for a Technical Corridor Entrance is on the shared Technical Corridors space. At the Encounter, discard all Noise markers in Corridors connected to the Room (including Technical Corridors if connected), draw a token, and place its matching Intruder in the Room. Keep a drawn non-Blank token aside outside the bag until a rule returns it. Compare its number with the triggering player's hand: Action and Contamination cards both count; fewer cards than the number causes a Surprise Attack against that player. If the token is Blank, no miniature appears; restore Noise to each connected Corridor. Contamination counts for this hand comparison but cannot pay Action costs.
answers.evidence: Noise roll and Technical Corridors: a second marker triggers an Encounter and Technical markers go on the shared space. Encounters and Combat quick reference specify clearing connected Noise, placing the matching miniature, setting aside non-Blank tokens, and counting Action plus Contamination cards for Surprise Attack.

answers.answer: Danger moves every neighboring Intruder that is not in Combat with a Character into the Room. If none are eligible, place a Noise marker in every connected Corridor that lacks one (including the Technical Corridors space if relevant). Intruder movement into a Character's Room is not an Encounter; the Intruder and Character are simply in Combat. A Character with Slime treats Silence as Danger.
answers.evidence: Exploration tokens and Noise roll: move all eligible Intruders; otherwise place Noise in each connected corridor lacking one. Encounters: an Intruder merely moving into a Character's Room is not an Encounter. Slime marker changes Silence to Danger.

answers.answer: In an Encounter, a Blank causes a Noise marker to be placed in each Corridor connected to the Room, and the Blank is returned to the bag. If it was the last token in the bag, add an Adult token if one is available. During bag development, drawing a Blank adds an Adult token if available (otherwise nothing happens) and returns the Blank to the bag; the summary does not state a last-token condition for that step.
answers.evidence: Encounters, Blank token: restore connected Noise; add an Adult only if Blank was the last bag token; return Blank. Intruder bag development: Blank adds an Adult if available and returns to the bag.

answers.answer: Both Intruders stay in the Room and destroy the Closed Door; multiple Intruders moving from the same Room destroy it simultaneously and all stay put. A destroyed Door lies down and cannot be closed again, except with the Plasma Torch Item. A Noise-triggered Intruder appearance is not blocked by a Closed Door.
answers.evidence: Door tokens: multiple Intruders trying the same Closed Door destroy it simultaneously and all stay; Destroyed Doors cannot be Closed again (except Plasma Torch); Noise-triggered appearances ignore Closed Doors.

answers.answer: The Intruder disappears into the ducts: remove its miniature, discard all its Injury markers, and return its token to the Intruder bag. The Noise marker on the Technical Corridors space remains. Characters cannot normally use Technical Corridors (the listed exceptions are the Mechanic's Technical Corridors Action card and Technical Corridor Plans Item); Door tokens can never be placed there.
answers.evidence: Technical Corridors: Intruders entering disappear, lose all injuries, and return to the bag; Noise stays. Characters have two specified exceptions; Doors can never be placed in Technical Corridors.

answers.answer: Both ordinary Shoot and Melee cost 1 Action card and target one Intruder in the Character's Room. Shooting also requires a Weapon in Hand with Ammo and discards 1 Ammo; a miss has no Melee miss penalty, and a double-hit result deals 2 Injuries (before Weapon modifications). Melee draws a Contamination card onto the Action discard pile before attacking; a miss inflicts 1 Serious Wound, and a two-hit result counts as only 1 Injury. Contamination does not pay the Action cost.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions: Shoot and Melee each cost 1; Combat: Shoot and Melee procedures specify same-Room target, Ammo, Contamination draw, miss effect, and two-hit result. Action Cost says Contamination cannot pay.

answers.answer: One Injury kills a Larva. For an Adult, draw one Intruder Attack card and compare its blood number to the Injury markers: it dies if blood is equal to or lower than injuries. For a Queen, draw two cards and add their blood values, then compare the total the same way. A dead Adult or Queen leaves an Intruder Carcass token in the Room; Larvae do not leave Carcasses. If a Queen's check draws a Retreat arrow, retreat overrides the numeric death check: draw an Event card, move the Queen through the corridor numbered in its Intruder movement section, and discard that Event card; either of the Queen's two cards can trigger retreat.
answers.evidence: Intruder Injuries and death; Intruder Retreat: Larva dies at 1 injury; Adult uses one blood check; Queen adds two blood values; dead non-Larvae leave Carcasses; retreat arrow replaces the numeric result, and either Queen card's arrow applies.

answers.answer: Before moving, resolve a separate Intruder Attack for each of the two Intruders. Escape attacks target the escaper. If the Character dies, their Corpse remains in the Room they tried to leave. If they survive, they complete the move to the neighboring Room; the unexplored Room is explored normally, and because it is empty they make a Noise roll after entering (unless its exploration effect suppresses the roll).
answers.evidence: Character Escape: one attack per Intruder before movement; death leaves Corpse in source Room; survival completes the move, with normal exploration/Noise rules. Intruder Attack identifies escaper as target.

answers.answer: Among Characters in the Intruder's Room, target the one whose player has the fewest Action cards in hand; break a tie by the First Player token, or the next player in turn order. Draw one Intruder Attack card: a matching Intruder type symbol is a hit, otherwise it misses. A Larva does not draw an Attack card: remove its miniature from the board, put it on the target's Character board, and give the target one Contamination card, placed on top of their Action discard pile.
answers.evidence: Intruder Attack and Infest (Larva attack): target selection, tie break, symbol match, and Larva procedure. Contamination cards: when gained, place atop Action discard pile.

answers.answer: Yes. Dressing a Serious Wound suppresses its effect but it still counts toward the three-wound limit, so at three Serious Wounds any additional Wound, including a Light Wound, kills the Character. Otherwise a third Light Wound clears the Light Wound track and causes a Serious Wound. Heal removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound as the healing effect specifies. On death, place a Character Corpse token in that Room and drop all the Character's Heavy Objects there.
answers.evidence: Character Wounds and death: third Light Wound converts to Serious; three Serious plus any additional Wound is death; dressing does not change the count; Heal and death placements are specified.

answers.answer: Canteen and Shower scan only Contamination cards in the Character's hand, removing all non-Infected ones; an Infected result places a Larva on the Character board, and if a Larva is already there the Character dies and a Creeper appears in the Room. Surgery scans every Contamination card in the deck, hand, and discard pile, removes all Infected cards and removes a Larva if present. It then causes 1 Light Wound, makes the Character automatically pass, and shuffles all their cards (including the hand and remaining Contamination) into their Action deck; their hand stays empty until next turn.
answers.evidence: Room Actions: Canteen/Shower scan hand; Surgery scans all zones, removes Infected cards and Larva, causes a Light Wound, auto-passes, and shuffles all cards. Contamination rules specify Larva and Creeper consequence.

answers.answer: Shoot or Melee against uncarried Eggs deals Injury markers, each of which destroys one Egg. Melee against Eggs never draws Contamination and a miss causes no Wound. A Grenade destroys 2 Eggs and a Molotov Cocktail destroys 1. Each Fire Damage step destroys 1 uncarried Egg in a burning Room. Make a Noise roll after every single attempt to destroy an Egg. When no Eggs remain in the Nest, it is destroyed and marked with 1 Injury marker.
answers.evidence: Eggs and the Nest: attacks, waived Melee penalties, grenade/Molotov values, Noise after every attempt, Fire damage, and Nest destruction are described.

answers.answer: Enter through the Evacuation Section A/B Room Action, paying 2 Action cards; the Pod must be Unlocked and have a free Character space in that Section. Resolve a Noise roll first. You cannot enter if an Intruder is present or appears, or if the Evacuation Section Room has a Malfunction marker. Each Pod carries up to 2 Characters, and Heavy Objects do not use Character spaces. After boarding, launch immediately or wait. While waiting, you may launch at the start of your first round in each Player Phase or exit for free; if you do not launch in your round, you automatically pass. If an Intruder appears in the Room, all waiting Pod occupants return to the Room. A second Character can immediately launch the waiting Pod with both aboard.
answers.evidence: Escape Pods and Room Actions: entry requirements, Noise/failure conditions, capacity, Heavy Objects, launch/wait/exit options, auto-pass, return on Intruder appearance, and second occupant launching are specified.

answers.answer: The Victory Check runs Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, then Objectives. With two Damaged Engines the ship explodes and everything aboard dies, including hibernating Characters and Intruders; launched Pods are already away. If the destination is not Earth, Characters hibernating aboard die, but the ship is not destroyed and Intruders do not die. The Quarantine Objective survivor is an exception when the destination is Mars. At Contamination, each surviving Character, including evacuated Pod passengers, scans all Contamination cards in their deck, discard, and hand. If at least one is Infected, shuffle all their Action and Contamination cards and draw four; any Contamination card among the four kills them. A Larva triggers this shuffle-and-draw-four directly without the initial scan. If neither infected cards nor Larva is present, no four-card test is needed.
answers.evidence: Victory Check: ordered steps and consequences for engines, coordinates (including Quarantine/Mars), contamination and Larva. It explicitly includes surviving evacuated Characters in the Contamination check.
